top_stories.title: OpenAI Employee Accounts Hacked via Chained Exploits Using Claude
points: Researchers (Hacktron AI) chained two critical vulnerabilities—an RCE (remote code execution, letting attackers run their own code on a server) bug in the libheif image library and a login flaw—to compromise employee ChatGPT/Codex accounts in July.

Compromised accounts gave access to internal OpenAI repositories, GitHub, Slack, email, and code systems; attackers used an employee's Codex (AI code-generation tool) to open a pull request in OpenAI's internal monorepo, proving full compromise.
Claude Opus 4.8 repeatedly failed to build a working exploit, but Claude Opus 5 cracked it within hours of release, alarming researchers about how fast AI is automating hacking.
Hacktron earned a $6,500 bug bounty for the disclosure.

unique_angles.point: Attackers reportedly used a version of Claude Opus 5 with loosened cybersecurity guardrails to execute the exploit.
The stark before/after between Opus 4.8 (failed) and Opus 5 (succeeded) is highlighted as evidence of rapidly accelerating AI hacking capability.

top_stories.title: Anthropic Quantifies Claude's Role in Its Own AI R&D
points: Anthropic reports Claude now completes about 26% of the company's AI research and development work end-to-end.
More than 30,000 AI agents perform research and engineering tasks simultaneously at any given time.
Staff collaborate with Claude on roughly 90% of their work, though Anthropic stresses humans maintain oversight and Claude is not operating fully autonomously.
Anthropic is building frameworks to track agent activity and proposed using a standardized automation rating scale (from Epoch AI) that other AI developers could adopt with independent verification.

unique_angles.point: Anthropic shared these metrics in a blog post specifically proposing three ways to measure AI progress industry-wide.

items.title: Safari Browser Gets Agent-Friendly MCP Support
points: Safari 27.0 (WebKit) ships 83 new features, headlined by Safari MCP (Model Context Protocol, a standard letting AI agents interact directly with software tools).

MCP lets AI agents control browser windows, manipulate the DOM (Document Object Model, the structured representation of a webpage's elements), inspect network requests, take screenshots, and read console output without user intervention.
This is expected to reduce friction for AI agents performing web-based tasks in real time.

items.title: Figure's Helix 2.5 Shows Zero-Shot Home Generalization
points: Figure's Helix 2.5 robot neural network tidied unfamiliar living rooms and folded towels across 30 different homes without task-specific training (zero-shot generalization).
The model trains on the Index dataset, which captures 35 minutes of human behavior footage every second globally, providing a constantly growing training pool.
Success suggests scaling data and compute directly improves robots' ability to handle new physical environments before deployment.

items.title: OpenAI's Emerging Agentic Software Factory
points: Codex agents now handle software changes from initial description through production: reading the codebase, Slack, and internal data, writing code, running tests, and opening pull requests until CI (continuous integration, automated testing) passes.

Specialized agent reviewers evaluate PRs by domain (cloud, infrastructure, security); low-risk changes get auto-approved while high-risk ones require human sign-off before a deploy agent ships and monitors them.
A 'Perf Factory' system monitors production performance, and 'Sevbot' (an incident-response agent) gathers context and suggests fixes during outages without auto-applying them.
The main constraint is cost: the heavy compute and token usage is currently affordable mainly for frontier AI labs, though this may become standard as token prices fall.

items.title: Jev: A Fast Scoring Model for New AI Tooling
points: Jev, built by ChatGPT co-inventor Diogo Almeida, scores possible outcomes in milliseconds instead of generating text sequentially like standard large language models (LLMs).
Early adopters have built model routers, PR reviewers, and context-compaction tools; one tool reduced a Claude Code session from 1 million tokens to 86,000 in one second.
Access is currently limited via a waitlist.

items.title: Claude Code Adds 'Projects' for Parallel Agent Coordination
points: Anthropic launched Projects (in beta) for Claude Code, letting developers coordinate multiple parallel AI threads within one session instead of managing separate contexts manually.
Each thread can delegate work to subagents with their own loops and workflows, and a main 'chief-of-staff' thread can hand off tasks to independent parallel cloud threads.
Threads can now reference, message, and monitor each other's progress—previously agents had no awareness of parallel work, forcing developers to copy context manually between sessions.

items.title: Meta's Luna Glasses Drop the Camera for Privacy
points: Meta's upcoming Luna smart glasses reportedly remove the camera entirely, replacing it with six microphones and a speaker in a thinner frame, addressing backlash over covert filming incidents in France and Australia.
Wearers interact via voice with Meta AI and 'Muse,' an always-ready AI assistant; a side button triggers Meta AI responses.
Rumored to ship in October, possibly announced at Meta's Connect conference September 23–24, in Clubmaster and Burbank styles.
Removing the camera doesn't fully resolve social-acceptability concerns, since six always-on microphones still raise audio surveillance questions.

items.title: OpenAI Foundation Funds $40M+ in Biomedical Datasets
points: OpenAI's nonprofit foundation's 'Data for Public Health' initiative granted $40M to a UNC–Chapel Hill program building personalized cancer-vaccine datasets, aiming to close the gap between large AI models and real biological research data.
It also backs OpenADMET competitions, which produce standardized datasets predicting how potential drugs behave in the human body (efficacy and safety profiles).
A separate $500K grant to nonprofit 1Day Sooner aims to rescue valuable research data from bankrupt biotech companies before it disappears.
Overall goal: give AI systems real medical training data rather than just publicly available information to pattern-match on.

items.title: Human Cortex Tissue Grown Inside Mice
points: Stanford researchers transplanted lab-grown human brain organoids (miniature human brain structures grown from stem cells) into mice missing most of their cortex; human tissue made up 90% of cortical volume within three months.
Transplanted neurons formed working connections with the mouse nervous system, extending fibers down to the spinal cord—the first time human brain cells integrated with a host animal this way.
Oxygen deprivation damaged some human tissue, giving researchers a living model to study cerebral palsy and similar brain injuries instead of relying on lab dishes.
Limitations remain significant: the tissue lacked normal cortical layering, and mice showed only partial improvement in memory and coordination compared to intact mice.

items.title: GLP-1 Drugs Used Off-Label for Pain and Inflammation
points: Doctors are prescribing GLP-1 drugs like semaglutide (originally for diabetes and weight loss) off-label to non-obese patients to treat pain and inflammation.
Evidence supporting this use remains preliminary.

items.title: Microsoft Executive Calls AI Training Practices 'Theft'
points: Unsealed court filings in The New York Times' copyright case against OpenAI and Microsoft reveal a top Microsoft director privately called AI training on copyrighted material 'the largest theft of labor in human history.'
Internal data showed Microsoft's Copilot reduced click-throughs to the Times' website by as much as 93%, indicating material business harm to publishers.
Filings allege OpenAI's training datasets contained over 91,000 copies of news outlet works, with staff planning to bypass paywalls undetected and strip copyright notices before training.

items.title: SpaceX Reportedly Buying Bankrupt Startups' Data to Train Grok
points: SpaceX is in informal talks to buy customer and operational data from failed startups, providing cheap training material for xAI's Grok models, which currently lag behind Anthropic, OpenAI, and Meta.
The approach mirrors Google's recent $10 million purchase of Spirit Airlines' business records at a bankruptcy auction.
Elon Musk says Grok 5, expected later this year, will integrate 25 years of SpaceX operational data, with an intermediate Grok 4.7 release planned for this month.

items.title: AI Leaders Invited to Trump-Xi Summit Dinner
points: Top AI industry leaders, including Qualcomm's CEO, have been invited to a Trump-Xi Jinping summit dinner on September 24.
Industry figures are reportedly pushing both leaders to adopt shared AI safety standards.
